lens: visual direction: specific, ambitious, drawable silhouette ideas that teach; moods, staging, transitions, teaching machines; kit feasibility
critical: FOUNDING PARITY NOW CONTRADICTS ITSELF (ch09-s04 vs ch12-s03). ch12-s03 says Anthropic's pin carries 'no name cards ... exactly as OpenAI's pin in ch09-s04 carries no names (both pins bare)'. But ch09-s04 still defines the founding grammar as 'a name card naming the founders' and shows the nameCard 'OpenAI · a non-profit · co-chairs Sam Altman and Elon Musk · research director Ilya Sutskever'. As written, OpenAI gets a founders card and Anthropic does not: a visible asymmetry in exactly the place the brief asks for even-handedness. FIX: choose one grammar and apply it word for word to both shots. Either (a) both pins bare, which means deleting ch09-s04's nameCard and the 'a name card naming the founders' clause (the founders are spoken in narration in ch12-s03; add 'OpenAI was founded, co-chaired by Sam Altman and Elon Musk' to L0909 only if the word budget allows), or (b) both get one equal-size founders nameCard in the same position, e.g. ch12-s03 'Anthropic · founded by Dario Amodei, Daniela Amodei and colleagues'. Also add a money ledger beat to ch09-s04 (or remove it from ch12-s03), so each founding gets the same objects: announcement, lantern pair, and ledger or no ledger.

ch14-s04 TINTS THE STRAIT emberRed, BREAKING THE CHAPTER'S OWN FAIRNESS RULE. ch14-s01 sets the rule for the whole chapter: both shores have 'no ... red tint' and 'always take exactly the same palette'. ch14-s04 opens on the right bank, with the Chinese officials and Liang, then sets 'the strait beyond is emberRed'. The film's one red-mood shot of the US–China chapter would then open on China's side. Viewers will read that as the very caricature the brief forbids, and it also spends the accent budget meant for the STATUS: OPEN stamp. FIX: shoot ch14-s04 in duskRose or winterBlue (the same mood as ch14-s03 is simplest). The market drop is carried by the falling ticker banner, and the match is carried by its own flare, the one warm practical in the reflection. If an alarm colour is wanted, put it only in the struck match's bloom, a practical, never in the strait.

THE kitWork LIST DOES NOT EXIST, BUT SHOTS DEPEND ON IT. ch08-s08b says 'KIT WORK (listed in the staging kitWork list; build it with a gallery entry before this shot is authored)', but staging has no kitWork key (keys: note, studyLock, caseBoard, questionThread, wallOfForecasts, candleClock, xrayColumn, hands, accentBudget, transitions, textRule, creditsSources). I re-checked docs/film/kit-catalog.md. lanternNetwork has no mask/maskSeed. transformerLoom is hard-wired to '1 causal head' with no causal:false and no two-loom layout (ch10-s10, ch10-s14). mistyHills has one fixed landscape and no lossF parameter (ch06-s03's convex bowl, ch08-s10's three lr cuts are not among the verified paths). nightLimb does not exist (ch01-s03, ch12-s06). There is no reflected-layer compositor for ch14's window-reflection candles (ch14-s01/s02/s04/s07). There are no props for the weir, ladle, balance scale, microscope, folding ruler, terrarium or hopper robot. FIX: add staging.kitWork with one line per extension, each with the shots that need it: lanternNetwork {mask, maskSeed, topology: custom layer sizes + fixed weights} (ch06-s06, ch07-s02, ch08-s08b, ch15-s08); transformerLoom {causal, halves:'encoder'|'decoder'|'both'} (ch10-s10, ch10-s14); mistyHills {lossF, lossDf, minima, lrSchedule} (ch06-s03, ch08-s10); sets/nightLimb (ch01-s03, ch12-s06); finish/reflection(layerFn, {alpha, flip:false, ripple}) as an offscreen study sub-render composited over the water (ch14); symbolic props weir, ladle, balanceScale, microscope, foldingRuler, terrarium, hopperRobot. Mark each as a blocking dependency for film-shots.

CHAPTER 14's REFLECTION DEVICE IS NOT ESTABLISHED ON SCREEN. Four shots put the candles, the match and the narrator's hands 'in reflection' in the study window over the strait. But no ch14 shot ever shows the window frame, so a viewer sees disembodied hands and candles floating over a harbour, with no cue that we are looking out through the study glass. ch13-s06 sets the device up once, a whole chapter (and 10+ seconds) earlier. FIX: every ch14 shot carries the study window's mullions as a faint L1 occluder at the frame edges (rim hairlines, candleAmber), so the strait is always seen THROUGH the study window. In ch14-s01, open the chapter on the window frame and push through it (FLAME PUSH-style, with no lamp change) before the wide of the two shores. Keep the reflection to one plane (L2, about 35% alpha, a slight ripple) so the hands read as reflection, not as giants over the water.

issues.where: ch11-s01, ch11-s03 (continuity after round-2 ch10 changes)
issues.problem: ch11-s01 opens with a 'Paper wipe ... from chapter 10's typesetter's case', and ch11-s03 calls nextToken 'the typesetter's case glimpsed at the end of chapter 10' and its context 'the same sentence chapter 10's threads lit'. After round 2, ch10-s14 explicitly shows 'no typesetter's case', and chapter 10's sentences are 'crossed the river bank' and 'I arrived at the bank after crossing the river'. Chapter 10 never lights 'The animal didn't cross the street…', so all three callbacks are now false.
issues.fix: ch11-s01: 'Paper wipe from ch10-s14's last frame (the board, the new thread-of-light card at C3-d)'. ch11-s03: delete 'glimpsed at the end of chapter 10' and replace 'the same sentence chapter 10's threads lit' with 'a new sentence (the kit's NEXT_TOKEN_DEMO)'. Keep the ghost-slot rhyme with ch10-s14's blank sort, which is real: 'the blank sort from ch10-s14 drops into this ghost slot'.

issues.problem: ch11-s08 says the chat box with its dark shears-shaped slot 'is not shown here'. ch12-s01 then opens 'Ink bleeds from chapter 11's dark shears-shaped slot', and ch12-s07 has the shears click 'into the dark slot seen at the end of chapter 11'. The slot is never seen before ch12, so the ink-bleed opens on an image the viewer has no context for.
issues.fix: Make ch12-s01's lead-in (1.2 s) open on the X-ray chat box in the study, with band 7 drawn as a dark shears-shaped empty slot, then ink-bleed from that slot to the Hopper stage. Change ch12-s07 to 'the dark slot seen at the start of chapter 12'.

issues.problem: On 'Turing's' the shot cuts to the case board, where 'Turing's child-machine card (filed in chapter 2)' glints in the manila file. Nothing of Turing's was ever filed: ch02-s05b pinned his forecast slip in W1 on the Wall. The board cut also happens inside a duskRose shot with no crossfadeMood, which breaks STUDY LOCK.
issues.fix: On 'Turing's', cut to the Wall: Turing's curled W1 slip (its child-slate pictogram from ch02-s05b now drawn small on its corner) glints. Add 'crossfadeMood duskRose→candleAmber 0.6 s over the cut (STUDY LOCK)'. Run the thread of light from W1 to the robot.

issues.problem: This is the round-2 issue, still open: the shot calls it 'the frayed candle MANY-LAYERED NETS ARE A STERILE EXTENSION'. Under the CANDLE-CLOCK RULE a frayed rim means a guttered candle, while this one is alive and goes out cleanly in ch05-s04.
issues.fix: Change it to 'the sterile candle MANY-LAYERED NETS ARE A STERILE EXTENSION (lit 1969, clean rim)'.

issues.problem: 'At the top of frame, the oxblood-thread question card ... unpins and drops slowly into the candle's pool' happens on the PAPER STAGE, but the question thread lives on the case board in the study. It is a geography break, and the stage has no thread.
issues.fix: Either cut it here and drop Q1 in ch05-s06 (the study, first beat: the hands unpin THEN HOW DO YOU TRAIN THE HIDDEN LAYER? into the lamp's pool, where it burns out), or show the board as a small window-inset over the stage. ch05-s06 is the cleaner choice, and it also lightens the 13-beat ch05-s04.

issues.problem: The transitionIn is lampChange, described as 'used here as the film's push-into-the-flame cue'. The kit's lampChange dims to BLACK for 1.5 s, while staging defines the flame push as 'never through black'. The two devices are being confused, and the shot also opens from the study board, not from a flame.
issues.fix: Set transitionIn to 'cut' (ch07-s01 ends in the study). Open ch07-s02 on the shelf: the FIDDLY candle's flame with its eleven-ring sleeve. Use the named FLAME PUSH (1.2 s push to lens 1.6, crossfadeMood candleAmber→dawnGold) into the stage. Then have Hinton light the warm-up candle from his hand-lantern, and in the hold show it appearing on the study shelf (a 1 s cutaway), because CANDLE PLACEMENT requires every belief candle to stand on the shelf.

issues.problem: ch09-s01 claims a 'Hard match cut (same serverCyan mood as chapter 8's last shot, so no lamp change)', but ch08-s14 is candleAmber. Its serverCyan is only the LED inset. A plain cut from amber to cyan pops the tint.
issues.fix: Make the match explicit: ch08-s14's last frame is the green LED inset pushed to full frame (crossfadeMood candleAmber→serverCyan over 0.8 s inside ch08-s14's hold). Then ch09-s01 cuts on the LED blink. Correct the sentence in ch09-s01.

issues.problem: The props list still names 'paper-cut panda', 'tissue veil of printed noise' and 'flip label', leftovers from a cut adversarial-example beat. A shot author working from props will draw them.
issues.fix: Replace the props with ['caseBoard', 'typewrittenAnnouncement', 'twoHandLanterns (warm, cold) on one pin', 'bankersLamp', and 'ledger' if parity option (b)].

issues.problem: (a) The props still say 'candle shelf running past the study window into the jetty rail', which contradicts CANDLE PLACEMENT (no jetty). (b) The visual says the candles stand 'in the order they were lit, left to right', but it also groups every still-lit candle 'at the shelf's right end'. LEARNED FEATURES (2012) was lit mid-shelf beside the expert and fiddly candles in ch08-s13b, and SMARTER-THAN-HUMAN (2023) was lit before the 2022 China candles in film order. The wax chart is the film's thesis image, and as written its layout is self-contradictory.
issues.fix: Fix the shelf strictly by year lit, as one left-to-right list in staging.candleClock, so the still-lit flames sit scattered among the dark sleeves. LEARNED FEATURES burns in the middle, after the 1999 and 2006 candles. The right end runs 2020 scale, 2022 chokepoint, 2022 one-to-three (dark), the 2025 match, the 2025 gap, then the 2023 worry candle placed by year, not by when it was filmed. The 'burning' pick-out on L1515 lights flames across the whole shelf, which teaches better than a cluster at one end. Delete 'into the jetty rail' from the props.

issues.problem: The visual promises a 'Music-only hold, about 12 seconds' with the CHM card up 'at least 11 seconds', but holdAfter is 7 and the card rises 0.8 s after 'better'. At 146 characters the text rule asks for about 13.7 s, so it gets roughly 7.
issues.fix: Either set holdAfter to 13, or cut the card to the fragment 'Before AlexNet, almost none … After it, almost all of them would.' (about 70 characters, 7.3 s) and keep holdAfter at 7. The second is better, since runtime is already over.

issues.problem: The film's grand reveal plays 'during the long lead-in', but leadIn is 4 s. Seven bands, each with an era date stamp, the shears clicking in at 3 s and the first card at 3.4 s come to about 0.5 s per band, far too fast to register what the film spent 25 minutes building.
issues.fix: Raise leadIn to about 10 s. Tilt at an even 1.1 s per band, with a soft chime per band (scored), shears at 8 s, first card at 9 s. Cut the date row from OST (the bands' own era typefaces carry it) to stay within the text rule.

issues.problem: Four windows at offsets 0, 1.2, 2.5 and 3.8 s, each with a date plus a 50–80-character caption ('a 'code red' declared by Google's management (reported, The New York Times)'). Each needs about 6–8 s by the text rule, but gets about 1.3. OST has 8 items.
issues.fix: Cut the captions to 2–4 words each, e.g. 'CODE RED (reported)', 'MICROSOFT · MULTIBILLION', 'LLaMA · LEAKED', 'GPT-4 · CLAUDE · SAME DAY', and space the windows 2.2 s apart, with the pause after 'stampede' raised to about 9 s. Move the full wording to creditsSources.

issues.problem: Round 2 flagged content filed under the 'date'/'nameCard' kinds, and it is still there. ch15-s05 has four 'date' items of 40–90 characters, e.g. 'ANTHROPIC · PIRATED BOOKS · $1.5 BILLION SETTLEMENT · APPROVED 20 JULY 2026', plus a 160-character court label. ch15-s04's METR label is about 190 characters and is read in a 4.8 s lead-in (needs about 17 s). ch14-s02 puts two quotes of about 175 characters up together (needs about 16 s each) inside a 41-word shot. ch14-s07 adds three unlisted rail pages. All exceed the 160-character cap.
issues.fix: Hard cap: a date stamp is place and date only (≤ 32 characters); a label is ≤ 70 characters. ch15-s05: tags become 'FEB–SEP 2026', 'JULY 2026', 'JULY 2026', 'SEP 2026'; court label 'Two courts, two rulings (Aug, Sep 2026)'. ch15-s04: 'METR · task length doubling ≈ every 7 months' plus the 1 HOUR / 16 HOURS pins as ruler lettering; the model names go to the sources card. ch14-s02: cut each quote to its operative fragment ('…used in military applications' / '…abuses export control measures…'), mirror-placed. ch14-s07: the rail pages become pictograms with years only ('2023 · 2024 · 2026').

issues.problem: Hassabis's puppet 'stands by the Wall beside it, in the light', inside the study. Until now no real person has entered the study, which is the detective's room where only the hands appear (Hinton's slip is taken down on the STAGE in ch13-s01, with the Wall as a stage backdrop). This breaks the film's spatial grammar.
issues.fix: In the study, only the hands pin W8 (the Wall's usual action). Hassabis appears on the stage after the crossfade, as a small figure inside the pool of SCALE IS THE MAIN LEVER, in the same tableau as the three Turing laureates, with his name card there.

issues.problem: An unresolved conditional is left in the shot text: 'beside it, if ch03-s09 shows him carrying it out, sits his small ADALINE shoebox'. ch03-s09 shows no shoebox (only an antenna), so a shot author cannot know what to draw. The props repeat the condition.
issues.fix: Delete the shoebox from ch15-s07 and its props. The lantern from Dartmouth carries 'Remember him' on its own. If an ADALINE plant is wanted, add it to ch03-s09 explicitly (Widrow carries a small needle-meter box toward the antenna, 3 s, wordless), then keep it here unconditionally.

issues.problem: On 'several', four cards 'fall onto the case board into the chapter's era column', inside a winterBlue Royal Institution shot with no crossfadeMood (STUDY LOCK), and the board map has no slots for these four blow-cards.
issues.fix: Stage the four equal cards falling onto the Lighthill lectern's desk inside the theatre (in-world, winterBlue), not onto the board. Alternatively add 'C1-w (four blow-cards, pinned ch04-s06)' to the staging slots and a 0.8 s crossfadeMood to candleAmber as the board comes in.

issues.problem: The X-ray beat lasts 'about two and a half seconds'. Round 2 lengthened ch07-s06 to 4.5 s for exactly this reason, and ch05-s10 gives 4–6 s. The shot also carries a walk-off, a gutter-out, a board pin, a thread to LEARNING, a flicker, a Mark I inset, a middle-layer inset and a book shadow, all within minDuration 17.
issues.fix: Hold the X-ray beat for 4.5 s (raise the pause after L0319 to about 4.5). Cut the 'Mark I two rows of wires' inset; ch03-s04 already showed that only the last knobs turn. Keep only the middle row of unlit lanterns with a question mark on 'middle layer'.

issues.problem: This is the densest non-deep-dive shot: office, 19-page calendar flip, two doubters with a quote card, pull-back to a globe, windows lighting, a market awning plant, a counter, a picture-tile tree, and the ImageNet plate, in about 20 s. Three text items besides stamp and name (quote, workers label, ImageNet label) break the text rule.
issues.fix: Cut the picture-tile tree (the 1,000-tile plate alone teaches 'categories') and the separate counter (the label carries the number). Fold the workers label into the ImageNet label: '≈ 50,000 workers · 167 countries → 1.2 M photos · 1,000 categories'.

issues.problem: Overloaded at about 17 s: an unexplained, unspoken 'THE BITTER LESSON · SUTTON · 2019' card (a riddle the viewer cannot decode), log-log paper, a night city with a 96-storey tower, a crane up to a flame, a match-cut to the shelf, the candle lit, a recipe tag, a pan to the Wall and a W4 glint.
issues.fix: Cut the Bitter Lesson card (or move it to creditsSources). Shorten the city to one beat: the ruled line tilts into the skyline and every window lights on 'error'. Keep the candle, the tag and the W4 glint.

issues.problem: Three text items besides name cards (the parrots title label, the two-accounts label, the Marcus quote), plus four name cards. The octopus/bear image is excellent but competes with the parrot, the two cards, Marcus and the board pin.
issues.fix: Drop the 'On the Dangers of Stochastic Parrots' label: the narration names it, and the parrot cut-out with its shuffled slugs is the label. Keep the two equal accounts cards and Marcus's fragment.

issues.problem: ch09-s01 has three labels besides the place stamp ('as reported by Cade Metz', '$44,000,000…', 'chose Google…'). ch03-s04 has three labels besides the date.
issues.fix: ch09-s01: merge them into two, 'as reported by Cade Metz' (whole shot) and 'stopped at $44M · chose Google · announced March 2013'. ch03-s04: drop '20 × 20 = 400 photocells'; ch08-s03 states it on screen later, where it pays off.

issues.problem: The Go candle A GO MACHINE IS A DECADE AWAY is never seen being lit; it first appears guttering out. A two-ring sleeve only reads as 'two years' if the viewer saw it start. The verb 'gutters out' also conflicts with the rule: a guttered candle is frayed, and this belief ended cleanly in 2016.
issues.fix: At 'guessed', a 1 s cutaway: the hands light the small Go candle on the shelf as the Coulom slip comes into focus (tag 2014). At the end, the candle goes OUT cleanly (no fray): flame snuffed, smoke thread, 2-ring sleeve, tag 2014–2016.

issues.problem: CHINA IS ONE TO THREE YEARS BEHIND 'gutters and goes out ... with a frayed rim', but staging lists it 'out January 2025' and the finale lists it without fray. Frayed means an uncertain end; this one is dated precisely.
issues.fix: It goes out cleanly when the match's draught blows it out: smoke thread, clean dark 2-ring sleeve, tag 2022–2025.

issues.problem: The visual says 'holdAfter 5, minDuration 18', but the fields are holdAfter 4.2 and minDuration 18. The visual also says the strip carries the 'statement's full text', while OST carries a trimmed fragment with an ellipsis.
issues.fix: Set holdAfter to 5, or edit the sentence. Make the strip the full one-sentence statement (it is short) and make the OST text identical to it.

issues.problem: 'A slow pan finds an empty space beside the lectern where a third figure is NOT: just a pool of light on the floor and an empty easel.' Nothing in narration or labels tells the viewer whose absence this is, so it is an undecodable riddle that costs about 2 s.
issues.fix: Cut the empty-easel beat and spend the time on the packed aisles and LeCun at the rear wall, which the label supports.

issues.problem: ch06-s07 calls the W6 slip 'planted here', but it was planted in ch01-s05. ch06-s08 threads to 'the Mark I's Buffalo card in column 1', which does not exist (C1-b is the knob card). ch05-s06's props list a 'magnifying glass' while the visual says 'no magnifier'.
issues.fix: ch06-s07: 'the 30-to-50-years slip (planted ch01-s05), corner only'. ch06-s08: 'to the 1958 knob card in C1-b'. ch05-s06: drop the magnifying glass from props.

issues.where: mood continuity on plain cuts (ch08-s02→s03→s04, ch11-s03→s05, ch11-s05→s07, ch12-s07→s08)
issues.problem: Several plain cuts jump between serverCyan and candleAmber with no practical motivating the change. The deep dive in particular ping-pongs: amber bedroom, cyan pixel plate, amber stencil plate, then gold cathedral. The staging transitions rule keeps tint changes for real mood changes.
issues.fix: ch08-s03: set the mood to candleAmber with the pixel grid's own glow as the practical (the bedroom lamp has just clicked off, so the LED-to-cell dissolve carries it). Elsewhere, change 'cut' to 'crossfade' where the mood differs, or add a 0.6 s crossfadeMood at the head of the incoming shot.

issues.where: chapter cards (ch02, ch03, ch04, ch07, ch09, ch11–ch15)
issues.problem: Only ch01-s07, ch05-s01, ch06-s01, ch08-s01 and ch10-s01 carry a chapter title. The case-file structure ('Clue One', 'Clue Two'…) is the film's spine, but most clue chapters never show their titles, so the viewer cannot see the clue count build.
issues.fix: Add one consistent, cheap device: a manila index tab typed with the chapter title (Special Elite) slides up out of the case file at frame bottom-left for 2.5 s at each chapter's first shot, over the existing picture, so no new shot is needed. Deep dives keep their full title cards.

issues.problem: The brief (user direction 2026-10-05) asks for a MID-LIFE narrator ('not an old-man voice', since the last film was 'sooo old'). The logline says 'An old teacher follows the case', and the hands are 'weathered', which steers casting and acting back toward old.
issues.fix: Logline: 'A teacher follows the case…'. The hands rig: 'steady, cuffed tweed forearms', with the signet ring kept and 'weathered' dropped. This is not a visual blocker, but the narrate stage reads the logline.

issues.problem: Summing leadIn, words at 2.0–2.3 words per second, pauses and holdAfter (with minDuration floors) gives about 35–38.5 minutes against a 32-minute target (brief maximum 35). Several fixes above add reading time.
issues.fix: Pay for the extra reading time by cutting on-screen text and density (the ch07-s03, ch11-s05 and ch12-s08 cuts above), not by adding holds. Trim narration words only where the picture already teaches: ch14-s07 L1421 (the three tags carry the voices), ch15-s05 L1525 (the terrarium carries it), and ch05-s04 L0520 (the family-tree tints carry it).

strengths: The core teaching machines are specific, drawable and bound to real numbers. The perceptron knobs turn only when the lit wires are wrong (ch03-s04). The scissors cannot separate XOR with one cut (ch04-s01). The messenger bead tugs strings by their real gradient (ch05-s04). The stencil lantern's worked 3.88 cell is verified against the kit (ch08-s04). The jug of light pours a real softmax (0.20 · 0.07 · 0.53 · 0.20, ch10-s06), and √d is taught by the jug slamming into one cup and frosting over (ch10-s07). A 3Blue1Brown viewer would recognise this level of rigour, rendered in paper.

Round-2 structural fixes landed. STUDY LOCK is now canonical and mostly obeyed, with named crossfadeMood crossings and era colour kept in practicals. The wax bar chart now matches the candle table (Cyc's 39-ring taper is the tallest dark bar and goes out wordlessly in ch13-s06). The PRE-TRAINING coat is tied on in ch07-s06 and recut in ch11-s01. Hassabis has his own cool practical rather than the doubters' rim (ch09-s03). ch10-s14 now ends on the curtain. The FLAME PUSH is defined once and reused.

The recurring grammar does real storytelling work. Believers stand in the light, doubters at the rim. Hinton's dissenter walk runs from the seated rim in 1976 to the centre in 2012 and back to the rim in 2023, with a ghost of his younger self (ch13-s02). The three lamps with overlapping pools replace a 'two teams' cliché (ch13-s04). The X-ray column lights one band per era and pays off all at once in ch12-s07.

Several images are genuinely new and memorable. In the Hall of Mirrors every reflected head is turned away (ch05-s01) and turns back for the Nobel (ch15-s01). The Winter Map pans east to west to a Helsinki window (ch04-s07). Dropout is lanterns snuffed by a real mask (ch08-s08b). RLHF is shears pruning a hedge (ch12-s02). The Bender–Koller octopus taps a telegraph cable while a bear appears (ch11-s08). The ImageNet labellers' globe goes dark on the day Mechanical Turk closes (ch15-s07). The final match is struck by a hand from the viewer's side (ch15-s09).

Fairness is written into the staging as visual rules, not just intentions: mirror-balanced shores with identical warmth and mirror-placed quote cards (ch14), identical lamps with equal stop times for each lab (ch15-s05), equal-size medallions for physics and chemistry (ch15-s01), and equal signatory silhouettes for three lab heads (ch13-s03). Most of the critical items above are places where the script drifted from its own good rules, not missing rules.
